question: Why cannot the great Lord of consciousness be described as limited in extent?
premises: The great Lord's nature is consciousness.
This point was stated clearly in the Prabodhapañcadaśikā.
inference: Because the great Lord is of the nature of immeasurable consciousness, he cannot truly be said to be limited.
plain_english: It cannot truly be said, because the great Lord, whose nature is consciousness, is immeasurable. I have stated this clearly in the Prabodhapañcadaśikā.
